message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles of the Napoleonic Wars.  Casualty figures vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are defined (killed, wounded, missing, captured).  A commonly cited estimate is:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **French** | ~25 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |
| **Allied (British, Dutch‑German, Prussian)** | ~22 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |

These totals include both killed and wounded, as well as soldiers who were taken prisoner or went missing.  Some historians give slightly higher or lower numbers—for example, the French may have suffered up to 30 000 casualties when including those who died later from wounds, while Allied losses might be quoted as 20–23 000.  

**Key points**

* The French army under Napoleon had roughly 73 000 men at the start of the battle; losing about 25 000 meant they lost roughly a third of their force.  
* The Allied coalition (primarily British, Dutch‑German, and Prussian troops) fielded about 68 000 men; losing about 22 000 meant they lost roughly a third as well.  
* The casualty figures illustrate why the battle was decisive: the French could not replace their losses quickly enough, whereas the Allies could bring in fresh troops from the Prussian reserve.

If you need more precise numbers from a particular historian or source, let me know!
